video_title: Tesco — Know What You're Sitting On
description: Timed to coincide with the school summer holidays, Tesco’s latest campaign from BBH London encourages customers to see their weekly shop as the gateway to getting away; whether on holiday, out for dinner or for a family day out. ‘Know what you’re sitting on’ shines a light on one of Clubcard's best kept secrets: the rewards customers could already be enjoying Tesco found that half a million of its Clubcard members are sitting on at least £100 to use with its Reward Partners. So, they decided to depict the scale of these discounts in a very literal way in a new campaign, running on TV and OOH as part of the ‘Need anything from Tesco?’ brand platform. The three films each focus on a different kind of Clubcard Reward. From a mountain of inflatables and sun umbrellas representing travel and holidays, to dining tables and chairs for restaurants and nights out, and a rollercoaster, for those family moments. Instead of creating these mountains of objects in post-production, the team, working with directors Glue Society, via Biscuit Filmworks, opted to build the sets from scratch, to demonstrate, in very real terms, the breadth of value Clubcard members could unlock. Murray Bisschop, UK Marketing Director at Tesco, said: “We know how easy it is for customers to focus on the great value that Clubcard Prices deliver and not notice their points and vouchers mounting up. We wanted to remind Clubcard members that the vouchers they are sitting on could be turned into big savings on holidays, meals out or days out. BBH have come up with a fun and engaging campaign that really brings that message to life for Tesco shoppers.” Gary McCreadie, Creative Director at BBH London, said: “It’s so easy to tap your Clubcard and not think about what you might be missing. This campaign captures the scale of Tesco discounts in a very real, dramatic, and hopefully unforgettable, way.” Each film points audiences to the Tesco app, with some of its well-known Reward Partners, including Hotels.com, PizzaExpress and Alton Towers Resort, shown on screen. The campaign is running on TV, VOD, DOOH, radio/audio and digital display in the UK. This  professional campaign titled 'Know What You're Sitting On' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Tesco, by ad agency: BBH London. This Film and OOH Outdoor media campaign is related to the Retail Services industry and contains 8 media assets. It was submitted 1 day ago.
why_ko: 소비자가 잊고 있던 클럽카드 포인트의 가치를 '무언가 위에 앉아 있다(sitting on)'는 관용적 표현을 활용해 실제 튜브, 의자, 놀이기구 등으로 만든 거대한 산으로 시각화한 아이디어가 뛰어납니다. CG 대신 실제 오브제 세트를 대규모로 실물 제작(Practical Set Building)하여 특유의 위트와 현실적인 중량감, 스케일을 확보했습니다. 추상적인 혜택의 크기를 직관적이고 거대한 실물 오브제로 치환하는 아트 디렉션 방식을 벤치마킹하기 좋습니다.
copy_ko: 당신이 무엇 위에 앉아 있는지 알고 있나요?
copy_note_ko: '혜택/돈을 묵혀두다'라는 의미의 영문 관용구 'sitting on'을 시각적 연출과 완벽하게 결합하여, 포인트 리워드의 규모를 일깨우고 행동을 유도하는 직관적인 중의적 훅입니다.

description: Cornett Launches ‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism VisitLEX invites visitors to for a “grounding” wellness experience they can only get in Lexington, KY on the “best ground in the world” Wellness seekers are spending thousands on retreats, cold plunges, and longevity supplements. Lexington, Kentucky has a simpler suggestion: touch grass. Specifically, Bluegrass. In collaboration with long-time partner Cornett, VisitLEX, the Lexington Convention and Visitors Bureau, today launches Bluegrass Bathing, a new destination-wide wellness experience that invites locals and visitors to kick off their shoes, settle into Lexington's iconic Bluegrass landscape and reconnect with nature. The concept draws inspiration from the growing popularity of “grounding,” also known as “earthing,” a wellness practice centered on making direct contact with the Earth's surface, allowing the body to absorb its natural electrical charge. According to recent medical reports, this connection can help improve sleep, lower stress levels, and reduce inflammation. “You can sit on the ground anywhere. But there’s something special about sitting on the same earth that nourishes the world’s best Thoroughbreds,” said Jonathon Spalding, Group Creative Director at Cornett. “Why touch regular boring grass when you can touch Bluegrass?” As the Horse Capital of the World, visitors are surrounded by more than 450 horse farms. Set among the rolling hills and lush green spaces that define Kentucky's Bluegrass Region, Bluegrass Bathing transforms one of Lexington's most recognizable natural assets into an immersive wellness experience. "If grounding is all about reconnecting with the Earth, then we're inviting folks to start their wellness journey with the best, most natural and nutrient-rich ground in America," said Mary Quinn Ramer, President of VisitLEX. "For centuries, these rolling hills have nurtured some of the world's most celebrated Thoroughbreds and the limestone water that runs beneath it has become the bedrock of our bourbon industry. But it’s also the way this Bluegrass makes you feel. Visitors consistently report they feel more relaxed the moment they touch down in Lexington. Bluegrass Bathing is our invitation to slow down, take a breath and experience the landscape that makes Lexington unlike anywhere else in the world." Visitors can “Bluegrass Bathe” at some of Lexington’s most iconic outdoor spaces, including a selection of Visit Horse Country farms and a handful of Lexington’s scenic parks (including Kentucky Horse Park, Gatton Park, and designated Parks & Rec locations). By booking at participating locations, guests will receive access to a series of curated wellness experiences including Pilates and sound baths along with a selection of guided meditations designed specifically for the program. Additionally, guests can deepen their connection to the Bluegrass by booking a dedicated tour of their host farm after the bathing experience. Each of the guided meditations was inspired by the natural elements that shape Lexington's landscape, encouraging participants to slow down, engage their senses and connect with their surroundings. VisitLEX has also produced a guided Sound Bath video set amidst a local horse farm and led by Amy Hudson, a certified Reiki master and sound healer from the Sound Healing Center of Lexington. To celebrate the launch, VisitLEX has also released a promotional video inspired by luxury wellness retreats. The video follows a solitary Bluegrass Bather enjoying a lush field of Bluegrass while a soothing narrator extols the virtues of one of Kentucky's most abundant natural resources. "We love creating experiences that could only happen in Lexington," added Ramer. "Bluegrass Bathing playfully reminds travelers that sometimes the best reset is simply being present and reconnecting our bodies with the Earth in a beautiful, natural setting. It's wellness, Kentucky-style." Visitors can learn more about Bluegrass Bathing at VisitLEX.com/Bluegrass-Bathing, where they can access all of the guided meditations, explore participating locations and discover additional wellness experiences throughout the destination. This  professional campaign titled '‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: VisitLEX, by ad agency: CORNETT. This Film medium campaign is related to the Travel and Tourism industry and contains 1 media asset. It was submitted 1 day ago.
why_ko: 유행하는 웰니스 트렌드인 '어싱(Grounding)'과 '산림욕(Forest Bathing)'을 재치 있게 뒤집어, 렉싱턴 특유의 블루그래스 잔디밭에 눕는 '블루그래스 베이딩'으로 재정의한 관광 기획입니다. 대중적인 라이프스타일 트렌드를 지역 고유의 자산과 결합하여 유쾌한 명분을 만들어내는 컨셉추얼한 프레임 재구성 방식을 훔칠 수 있습니다. 값비싼 웰니스 리트릿 대신 '진짜 좋은 땅을 밟으라'고 말하는 수사법과 브랜드 위트가 돋보입니다.
copy_original: Why touch regular boring grass when you can touch Bluegrass?
copy_ko: 왜 지루하고 평범한 잔디를 밟나요, 블루그래스를 밟을 수 있는데?
copy_note_ko: 자연과 접촉한다는 웰니스 용어 'Touch Grass' 및 '어싱' 트렌드를 렉싱턴 고유의 블루그래스(Bluegrass) 잔디 품종과 언어유희로 결합하여 지역 관광의 차별점을 드러낸 위트 있는 카피입니다.

video_title: BOOKSY — Dallas Beauty Pros Bring Pet Portraits to Life at Sit. Stay. Style.
description: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/6QmcgkSszZc Booksy and Humanaut Help Dallas Beauty Pros Bring Pet Portraits to Life at Sit. Stay. Style. Booksy has teamed up with creative agency partner Humanaut to host a live, pop-up pet studio in Dallas that shows how the booking app helps beauty and wellness providers build and grow thriving businesses – regardless of their focus or area of expertise. To bring that brand promise to life, the global beauty booking app tapped Humanaut to help it create Dallas’s most specific beauty studio. Called “Sit. Stay. Style.,” the one-day pop-up event took place in Dallas’s Deep Ellum neighborhood and featured local beauty and creative service professionals who treated guests to hair, nail, and tattoo art services that were inspired by their pets. Prior to the event, Humanaut created a short teaser video and static social assets, which Booksy used to drive awareness and fill bookings. One teaser encouraged local pet parents to book an appointment for “your pet’s portrait on you.” Four participating beauty and wellness businesses also created and posted their own social teaser videos to further amplify the pop-up. On the actual day, these providers – Color & Curls, Nailed By Daniela, Annie’s Acrylics, and Lilac Tatto Studio – pampered pet owners with intricate temporary hair, nail and tattoo art inspired by portraits of attendees’ pets. No matter how specific or unique the portrait (in one case, an attendee got a tattoo of their pet tarantula), these four beauty providers delivered – and all appointment slots, powered by Booksy, were fully booked leading up to the event. The pet-themed pop-up was decked out in all things pets and also featured a custom pet portrait coffee cart that printed pet-inspired art right on top of lattes. “We handled everything from space design to artist sourcing to building out a fully operational salon space, staffed with professional tattoo, hair, and nail artists in a very short amount of time. Every detail — from the waiting area to the artwork on the wall — was built around a single emotional hook: people's love for their pets,” said Chad Harris, Senior Producer at Humanaut. “To bring this concept to life we decided to focus on a single super specific theme for our talented providers to bring to life: pet portraits. Dallas’ love for pets is as big as everything else in Texas, so we wanted to give pet owners a fun way to express their love,” said Bethany Maxfield, Executive Creative Director at Humanaut. The pop-up builds on a larger-than-life, guerrilla marketing-inspired billboard stunt that Humanaut created for Booksy as a part of its launch in Dallas earlier this summer. Humanaut is an independent creative and production company based in Chattanooga. This  professional campaign titled 'Dallas Beauty Pros Bring Pet Portraits to Life at Sit. Stay. Style.' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: BOOKSY, by ad agency: Humanaut. This Experiential medium campaign is related to the Professional Services industry and contains 1 media asset. It was submitted about 1 hour ago.

description: Quilter, the wealth management company, has partnered with independent creative agency Joint to bring its 'Money Needs a Plan' platform to television for the first time, marking a major new chapter for the campaign and the brand's biggest push yet. Developed by Joint, the campaign encourages people to think differently about their money and whether it's simply sitting doing nothing for them. Working in a category often associated with inertia, Joint set out to create a campaign that would feel simple, relatable and relevant to everyday life. Rather than leaning into fear or financial complexity, the creative uses humour to completely reframe people's relationship with money. The campaign marks Quilter's first-ever TV advertising campaign and its biggest brand investment to date. Running for five weeks across TV, BVOD, social and digital channels, the hero film is directed by Tim Godsall, whose acclaimed comedic storytelling brings warmth and relatability to the campaign's central message. Media planning and buying has been led by Bountiful Cow, whose strategy combines the broad reach and emotional impact of premium broadcast television with precision audience targeting to ensure Quilter reaches affluent consumers in trusted, high-attention environments. Launching across Sky, Channel 4 and broadcaster video-on-demand, the campaign uses ONS postcode data to focus activity in affluent areas nationwide, while premium programming including The House of Dragon, Rob & Romesh Vs, Formula 1 Highlights and live Premier League football, Formula 1 and cricket was carefully selected to place Quilter's message alongside content that resonates with its audience. Beyond linear TV, the strategy extends Quilter's storytelling through 40-second VOD creative across ITVX, Amazon and Channel 4, giving the brand more time to build understanding while retaining the premium context, targeting and addressability of broadcaster platforms. By combining broad reach with richer storytelling in trusted viewing environments, the campaign creates a Relative Advantage that helps Quilter stand apart in a category where trust and consideration are critical. Alongside AV, Quilter will bring the campaign to life with new digital executions shot by James Day. The campaign also extends across Meta, LinkedIn and Reddit, with each platform playing a distinct role within the customer journey. Reddit, in particular, enables Quilter to engage financially engaged communities actively researching, discussing and seeking advice on major financial decisions, allowing the brand to participate in relevant conversations at moments of genuine consideration rather than interruption. Jo Harris, chief customer officer at Quilter said, “Most people have things they want to achieve in life, whether that's buying a home, supporting their family, retiring comfortably or simply feeling more in control of their finances. But those goals can be much harder to reach without a plan.” “This campaign is all about helping people see that financial planning doesn't have to be complicated or only for the wealthy. It's about having a clear idea of where you want to get to and taking practical steps to move in the right direction.” “By taking Money Needs a Plan to TV for the first time, we will reach more people with a simple message that whatever matters to you in life, having a plan for your money can help you get there.” Algy Sharman, chief creative officer at Joint added, "It has been so rewarding to see how this brand platform can extend into other channels, including some fantastic new digital and experiential work as well as Quilter's first ever TV spot. It is smart, funny but most importantly persuasive." George MacKean, Business Director at Bountiful Cow, said: “Quilter's first TV campaign required a media strategy that balanced broad reach with smart audience targeting. Premium broadcast delivers the scale, trust and emotional impact needed to introduce the brand to a wider audience, while our digital strategy allows us to continue that conversation in environments where people are actively thinking about their financial future. "Rather than relying solely on demographic targeting, we focused on reaching people in the right contexts and mindsets. Reddit gives Quilter a Relative Advantage because it's still an underutilised platform for financial services brands, allowing Quilter to directly engage communities in moments of genuine consideration instead of competing for attention in crowded channels. It’s an approach that ensures Quilter isn't just reaching the right audience but reaching them when they're most receptive to thinking differently about their money." This  professional campaign titled 'Money Needs a Plan' was published in United Kingdom in July, 2026. It was created for the brand: Quilter, by ad agencies: Bountiful Cow and Joint. description: Monzo has launched ‘Get busy living’, its first global brand platform, as the bank looks to build on its growth across the UK and Europe. The campaign focuses on the idea that when managing money becomes effortless, people have more time to focus on the things they enjoy. It reflects Monzo’s evolution from a fintech challenger into a mainstream bank serving more than 15 million customers and businesses, with services spanning budgeting, saving, borrowing, investing, mortgages and retirement planning. Developed by BBH London with Monzo’s in-house creative studio and NUSA STUDIOS, the campaign is Monzo’s biggest integrated brand campaign to date. Directed by Daniel Wolfe, it features 10 cinematic single-shot films depicting everyday moments, from making a daughter laugh at bathtime to singing in the driver’s seat of a van. Monzo’s products appear subtly within each story, showing how features such as Salary Sorter, Joint Accounts and Monzo for Under 16s can handle financial tasks in the background while customers focus on life. Narrated by Olivia Colman and soundtracked by tracks including ‘Teenage Dirtbag’, ‘Careless Whisper’, ‘Baba O’Riley’ and ‘Days Like This’, the campaign combines warmth, humour and optimism to reinforce Monzo’s broader mission of making money work for everyone. The platform spans TV, cinema, SVOD, BVOD, radio, social, digital and out-of-home, with media planning by Starcom. The OOH campaign includes major placements at Waterloo Motion and Piccadilly Lights, featuring photography by Elliot James Kennedy. This  professional campaign titled 'Get busy living' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Monzo, by ad agency: BBH London. description: AB InBev has launched ‘Cheers to Beer’, a new global campaign created with Wieden+Kennedy ahead of International Beer Day on August 7. The campaign celebrates the role beer has played in bringing people together across cultures and generations, highlighting the everyday occasions where a simple cheers can represent celebration, comfort, gratitude, encouragement or connection. The campaign is anchored by a global film that showcases a wide range of moments where beer acts as a catalyst for community and belonging. Building on AB InBev’s 2021 ‘Let’s Grab a Beer’ campaign, the new work focuses on what beer can represent once people come together, from intimate everyday gatherings to major sporting events. The campaign is supported by research from Ipsos and IWSR showing beer’s continued strength among legal-drinking-age consumers, as well as growing interest in moderation and no-alcohol options. The launch follows AB InBev’s Q2 2026 results, which showed continued growth across its beer portfolio. Beer revenue increased 5.6%, while beer volume grew 1.1%, with no-alcohol beer up 27%, Beyond Beer up 44% and its Balanced Choices portfolio up 13%. Together, the campaign and results position beer as a category that continues to adapt to changing consumer preferences while maintaining its longstanding role in social connection. video_title: Weight Watchers — Here At Every Point’
description: Weight Watchers has launched ‘Here At Every Point’, a 60-second film directed by Martina Magorin of Golden LA that takes a more personal approach to the weight loss category. Created with Anomaly, the film follows a woman who, between work and motherhood, has gradually lost touch with an earlier version of herself. When she discovers a favourite pair of jeans and an old Polaroid, she begins reflecting on her journey through false starts, small victories and early-morning weigh-ins. The campaign is designed to speak to the growing GLP-1 landscape while positioning Weight Watchers as a broader support system that combines nutrition, coaching, medication and community. Rather than focusing solely on physical transformation, the film centres on accountability, connection and helping people rediscover confidence in their everyday lives. Magorin describes it as a story about finding your way back to the version of yourself that feels comfortable enough to say yes and fully enjoy life. Magorin and director of photography Sean Conaty used an intimate visual approach, relying on eye-level framing, simple locked-off shots and gentle handheld camera work to keep the focus on the character and performance. The wardrobe also evolves throughout the story, moving from layers and softer shapes that help the character hide towards more colourful and intentional clothing that reflects her growing confidence. ‘Here At Every Point’ is rolling out nationally across broadcast, digital and social platforms. This  professional campaign titled 'Here At Every Point’' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Weight Watchers, by ad agency: Anomaly. description: Built around the universal habit of pressing an almost-finished bar of soap onto a new one, the campaign transforms a familiar household ritual into its central idea. Rather than focusing on product benefits or beauty claims, it celebrates the behaviour itself, using the relationship between old and new soap bars as a playful metaphor for staying connected and making the most of what remains. The film follows this simple but relatable insight through a light-hearted narrative, turning an everyday act of thrift and practicality into an emotional story. By elevating a behaviour that millions of people recognise, the campaign finds meaning in a small domestic habit that is rarely acknowledged in advertising. The story culminates in a memorable visual of leftover soap fragments fused to a fresh bar, reframing what is often considered waste as something valuable. In doing so, the campaign highlights themes of continuity, resourcefulness and everyday ingenuity, celebrating the simple ways people maximize every last bit of a product. description: Commissioned by UN Women, Bystander is a tense, intimate short film exploring the split second where instinct, fear and responsibility collide. Across a series of everyday settings - a bus stop late at night, a locker room after a match, an online gaming session, an open-plan office - we witness subtle but recognisable moments of harassment and boundary-crossing behaviour directed towards women. Nothing heightened. Nothing dramatised beyond reality. Just the familiar discomfort of something not quite right. Each character faces the same internal question: intervene, or stay silent? Told through restrained performances, tightening frames and immersive sound design, the film places the audience inside the pause before action, where rationalisation and conscience wrestle for control. Rather than judging its characters, Bystander examines the psychology of inaction in the face of harassment and abuse towards women and the quiet realisation that silence, too, has consequences. This  professional campaign titled 'BYSTANDER' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: UN Women UK, by ad agency: Media Trust. description: Did you spot all these cameos in 'What has the BBC ever done for me?' A skeptical viewer questions the value of the BBC, leading to a journey through iconic shows, programs, and radio services. This fast-paced exploration highlights the breadth of BBC content, from news and drama to nature documentaries and entertainment, while examining the corporation's overall impact on British culture and the economy. Romesh Ranganathan is asking the big question, ‘What has the BBC ever done for me?’ He begins by asking a star-studded Queen Vic pub, complete with Coldplay’s Chris Martin on piano. Romesh travels through Albert Square, Casualty, BBC News, Radio 1Xtra, Graham Norton’s studio, Wimbledon, ending up on stage in Strictly Come Dancing. Along the way he meets Claudia Winkleman and some Traitors, Alan Carr, Daleks, Ruth Jones as Gavin & Stacey’s Nessa, Hey Duggee and Anton Du Beke. There is a BBC for each of us, funded by all of us. description: Confused.com and Leo UK are bringing some of the nation’s most familiar sayings to life in a new campaign capturing the disproportionately good feeling of having Just Used Confused.com. ‘Feels like…’ is the latest chapter of the award-winning brand platform, which celebrates the fleeting sense of triumph that comes from conquering life admin, saving some money and feeling, briefly, like a fully functioning adult. The 2025 instalment of the platform won multiple Golds at Creative Circle and British Arrows, including the prestigious John Webster Award. Each film begins in the real world as someone finishes sorting their insurance with Confused.com. Their relief triggers a comedic cutaway into a heightened world where the feeling is expressed through a familiar idiom, interpreted very literally by a cast of handcrafted animal puppets. The environments and supporting characters were developed and enhanced with AI production tools. In ‘The Cat That Got the Cream’, a man sorting his car insurance cuts to an ageing, bespectacled cat in a supermarket. After seriously considering whether he deserves a pot of cream, the cat drops it into his basket and reasons: “Cream, double cream! That’s coming home with me that, Meow.” ‘Laughing ’til the Cow Comes Home’ introduces Pig and Sheep, two laid-back former university housemates enjoying an afternoon of doing very little while Cow is at his nine-to-five. Pig is midway through a joke when Cow appears in the doorway, briefcase in hand, and shouts: “Oh please don’t stop on my account...” Completing the trio is ‘The Early Bird That Got the Worm’, starring a polished and profoundly pleased-with-herself blue tit. Carrying a shopping bag emblazoned with a worm, she struts past a queue of less fortunate birds and announces: “you should’ve set your alarms”. The characters were developed with BlinkInk stop motion directing duo, Andy Biddle and Adeena Grubb, with every detail designed to build their personalities, from the cat’s increasingly necessary reading glasses to Cow’s carefully pressed workwear, and the early bird’s jumper draped deliberately over her shoulders. Biddle was a lead animator on Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs, while Grubb is a multi-award-winning puppet maker and animation director. Their combined experience in handcrafted filmmaking helped bring the campaign’s familiar idioms to life through characters packed with charm, wit and sharply observed detail. Each film ends with the line, “Insurance feels better when you’ve just used Confused.com”, followed by the familiar Confused.com whistle, performed by its respective puppet character. First introduced with the launch of the ‘Just Used Confused.com’ platform, the whistle has since grown into an established sonic asset for the brand. The campaign will be supported by ten and six second edits, alongside radio and social activity, and will run across TV, BVOD, social and radio in the UK from 7th August. The campaign was developed with Zenith, which led media planning and buying. Together, the team delivered an integrated campaign with an effective media mix, designed to elevate the Just Use Confused.com platform and build fame nationwide. It’s almost impossible to pick a favourite, but Angry Cow has to take the top spot. He was inspired by Mark from Peep Show, while the pig took plenty of cues from Jeremy. We even snuck in Mark’s iconic creamy elephant sofa and named the characters Mark Cowigan, Jeremy UsPork and Super Lamb. If you’re familiar with Peep Show, you’ll understand why. If you’re not… go and watch Peep Show. This  professional campaign titled 'Feels like…' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. description: Cornett Launches ‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism VisitLEX invites visitors to for a “grounding” wellness experience they can only get in Lexington, KY on the “best ground in the world” Wellness seekers are spending thousands on retreats, cold plunges, and longevity supplements. Lexington, Kentucky has a simpler suggestion: touch grass. Specifically, Bluegrass. In collaboration with long-time partner Cornett, VisitLEX, the Lexington Convention and Visitors Bureau, today launches Bluegrass Bathing, a new destination-wide wellness experience that invites locals and visitors to kick off their shoes, settle into Lexington's iconic Bluegrass landscape and reconnect with nature. The concept draws inspiration from the growing popularity of “grounding,” also known as “earthing,” a wellness practice centered on making direct contact with the Earth's surface, allowing the body to absorb its natural electrical charge. According to recent medical reports, this connection can help improve sleep, lower stress levels, and reduce inflammation. “You can sit on the ground anywhere. But there’s something special about sitting on the same earth that nourishes the world’s best Thoroughbreds,” said Jonathon Spalding, Group Creative Director at Cornett. “Why touch regular boring grass when you can touch Bluegrass?” As the Horse Capital of the World, visitors are surrounded by more than 450 horse farms. Set among the rolling hills and lush green spaces that define Kentucky's Bluegrass Region, Bluegrass Bathing transforms one of Lexington's most recognizable natural assets into an immersive wellness experience. "If grounding is all about reconnecting with the Earth, then we're inviting folks to start their wellness journey with the best, most natural and nutrient-rich ground in America," said Mary Quinn Ramer, President of VisitLEX. "For centuries, these rolling hills have nurtured some of the world's most celebrated Thoroughbreds and the limestone water that runs beneath it has become the bedrock of our bourbon industry. But it’s also the way this Bluegrass makes you feel. Visitors consistently report they feel more relaxed the moment they touch down in Lexington. Bluegrass Bathing is our invitation to slow down, take a breath and experience the landscape that makes Lexington unlike anywhere else in the world." Visitors can “Bluegrass Bathe” at some of Lexington’s most iconic outdoor spaces, including a selection of Visit Horse Country farms and a handful of Lexington’s scenic parks (including Kentucky Horse Park, Gatton Park, and designated Parks & Rec locations). By booking at participating locations, guests will receive access to a series of curated wellness experiences including Pilates and sound baths along with a selection of guided meditations designed specifically for the program. Additionally, guests can deepen their connection to the Bluegrass by booking a dedicated tour of their host farm after the bathing experience. Each of the guided meditations was inspired by the natural elements that shape Lexington's landscape, encouraging participants to slow down, engage their senses and connect with their surroundings. VisitLEX has also produced a guided Sound Bath video set amidst a local horse farm and led by Amy Hudson, a certified Reiki master and sound healer from the Sound Healing Center of Lexington. To celebrate the launch, VisitLEX has also released a promotional video inspired by luxury wellness retreats. The video follows a solitary Bluegrass Bather enjoying a lush field of Bluegrass while a soothing narrator extols the virtues of one of Kentucky's most abundant natural resources. "We love creating experiences that could only happen in Lexington," added Ramer. "Bluegrass Bathing playfully reminds travelers that sometimes the best reset is simply being present and reconnecting our bodies with the Earth in a beautiful, natural setting. It's wellness, Kentucky-style." Visitors can learn more about Bluegrass Bathing at VisitLEX.com/Bluegrass-Bathing, where they can access all of the guided meditations, explore participating locations and discover additional wellness experiences throughout the destination. This  professional campaign titled '‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: VisitLEX, by ad agency: CORNETT. video_title: American Pecan Promotion Board — “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans”
description: The American Pecan Promotion Board (APPB) is bringing back its “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans” campaign for a third round, once again teaming with ad agency Signal Theory and creative studio SixTwentySix. The new spots keep the campaign’s signature comedy going, highlighting the everyday moments when pecans are the right call. The third installment of “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans” features three spots built around everyday moments when a pecan snack becomes essential: “Move In”: A father drops his daughter off at college for an emotional goodbye, both wishing Mom could be there. She is, as it turns out, in the car the whole time snacking on pecans. “Drop Off”: A mother tries to get her son to school on time, only to be stopped by a crossing guard who takes pecan snacking very seriously. “Snack Break” (to debut later in 2026): A group of office coworkers speculate about a colleague’s frequent trips outside, unaware she is sneaking away for a pecan fix. “This year we pushed the snack break to feel less casual and a lot more urgent. It’s that moment when you need a snack before you break, and we’ve all been there,” said Joe Wilper, executive creative director at Signal Theory. “The spots lean fully into pecans as the healthy escape you needed at exactly the right moment. Whether it’s the long wait at school pickup, college move-in day or the excuse to finally get up from your desk, we’re reminding people that reaching for pecans is the smart snack in surprising moments.” The new spots mark the third collaboration between Signal Theory and SixTwentySix, led by director Evan Bourque. The partnership has grown tighter with each round, with Signal Theory crediting close creative alignment between both teams for keeping production efficient and the work sharp. "Our goal with these spots was to make them feel like snippets from a movie rather than a commercial, so every choice, from casting to locations to lighting, was built around that idea," said Evan Bourque, director at SixTwentySix. "It's always a pleasure working with the creatives at Signal Theory. They write fun scripts and stay open to new ideas, which makes the end result stronger. The characters are really what make these spots stand out, a quirky character paired with a grounded one, keeping things entertaining." This  professional campaign titled '“Surprisingly Snackable Pecans”' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: American Pecan Promotion Board, by ad agency: Signal Theory. This Digital and Film media campaign is related to the Food industry and contains 2 media assets. description: Canva has launched its first large-scale brand campaign in Thailand, ‘Anyone Can with Canva’, positioning AI-powered video editing as an accessible tool for everyday creativity rather than a skill reserved for professional filmmakers or agencies. Created in partnership with acclaimed Thai filmmaker Nawapol Thamrongrattanarit, the campaign reflects the growing influence of short-form video across Southeast Asia and encourages a wider range of people to participate in visual storytelling. The hero film takes place inside a chaotic advertising agency struggling through endless client revisions before an unlikely group of editors, including a delivery rider, security guard and cleaner, step in to transform the project using Canva’s video editing tools. With its humorous and distinctly local tone, the campaign embraces the idea that creativity can come from anyone, regardless of professional experience, and highlights how technology is lowering barriers to content creation. A key element of the initiative is giving the public access to licensed footage from Thamrongrattanarit’s personal archive, allowing users to experiment with professional-quality material using Canva’s AI-powered editing tools and templates. The campaign also supports Canva’s broader growth strategy in Thailand, where the company has expanded its presence through partnerships such as its education initiative with the Office of the Basic Education Commission, helping bring Canva for Education to millions of students and teachers across the country. This  professional campaign titled 'Anyone Can' was published in Thailand in June, 2026. It was created for the brand: Canva Thailand, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. description: Wolf BKK has partnered with Pruksa to launch an unconventional campaign for the property developer’s new premium residences by presenting a home as if it were the world’s most valuable gadget. Priced at 25 million baht, the campaign taps into society’s fascination with new technology, suggesting that the greatest innovation in improving everyday life may not be a device at all, but a thoughtfully designed home. The campaign began by teasing a mysterious premium gadget through billboards, digital screens, social media and online films, promoting it as a breakthrough invention with life-changing capabilities. As curiosity grew, audiences speculated that the product could be an advanced AI system or another futuristic technology capable of justifying its multimillion-baht price tag. The final reveal showed that the advertised features had never belonged to a gadget, but were the everyday benefits of a home. By disguising a premium residence as a piece of cutting-edge technology, Pruksa reframed its property launch as a conversation about value, challenging people’s obsession with the latest innovations while reminding them that a home remains one of the most meaningful investments in making life easier, smarter and more comfortable. This  professional campaign titled 'The Most Valuable Gadget in the World' was published in Thailand in July, 2026. It was created for the brand: Pruksa, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. description: Today, The Coca‑Cola Company announces the launch of ‘Fizz or Sizz’, a playful, insight‑led campaign that transforms a familiar sensory moment into a mass participation experience. Set in Japan, where fried chicken is hugely popular but not instinctively paired with Coca‑Cola, the campaign is built around a simple but surprising truth: the sound of Coca‑Cola fizzing is almost indistinguishable from the sound of karaage sizzling. By making sound the creative hero, ‘Fizz or Sizz’ turns this uncanny similarity into a nationwide guessing game — asking people one deceptively simple question: is it sizz or fizz? Rolling out across radio, digital out‑of‑home and social media, the campaign invites audiences to listen and engage in real time. Correct guesses can reward participation with a chance to win a free Coke, daily over the course of the week‑long activation. Rather than delivering a traditional product message, ‘Fizz or Sizz’ uses play, sound and immediacy to draw people into a broader cultural conversation about food, taste and refreshment. By gamifying the fizz of Coca‑Cola and placing it alongside the sizzle of freshly cooked food, the campaign subtly rewires cultural associations — making the two sensations feel inseparable in people’s minds. The activation also demonstrates how mass media can feel participatory at scale. Across radio, outdoor and social channels, audiences are invited to actively take part rather than passively observe, creating a shared moment that feels intuitive, accessible and highly shareable. Tish Condeno, Senior Director, Coca‑Cola Trademark Category, Coca‑Cola Japan said: “Sound has a way of triggering recognition in an instant. ‘Fizz or Sizz’ brings together two familiar noises that often blur together, inviting you to listen closely to the crackle of food and the first response of a drink opening or being poured. The result is a light, interactive moment for Coke lovers rooted in food and refreshment.” ‘Fizz or Sizz’ will run across Japan via radio, OOH, social and in‑store engagement touchpoints. The campaign was developed by WPP Open X, led by Grey, supported by Ogilvy, WPP Production, and WPP Media. This  professional campaign titled 'Fizz or Sizz' was published in Japan in April, 2026. It was created for the brand: Coca-Cola, by ad agency: WPP Open X, led by Grey, supported by Ogilvy, WPP Production, and WPP Media..
